state:
Goal `core-response-and-1-more`: nine of `Core\Response`'s ten members carry every feature proof. The
nine are `addCookie`, `bytes`, `html`, `text`, `json`, `setStatus`, `setHeader`, `redirect` and
`sendFile`. Each has `about.md`, three examples with `.nvsr` requests, the attack, the bench record in
`docs/perf/members.ndjson`, and a `covers:` line in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs`'s `tests`
module. Their cards follow AGENTS.md § *Text an end user reads*. `stream` owes every proof, and its
card is not plain yet. `Core\Response\Stream` is still in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`, and
`Core\Response\Stream::write` owes every proof. Nothing is blocked.

`nvs run --request` prints the response body alone, never the status line or the headers, so an
example about a status or a header shows it through the body it writes. A file `sendFile` named is
written after the program ends, when it ended without an error, which is what a server does
(`crates/nvs-cli/src/main.rs`'s `send_file_body`). A body member's bench writes bodies with no
newline in them, because a newline flushes the terminal on every call. The wall-clock of these
benches is noisy: compare the allocation and byte counts. `benches/members/core/Response/nvs.toml`
grants `fs.read` over that folder for the `sendFile` bench, and every Response bench runs under it.

items.text: **`Core\Response::stream`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, Rust `covers:` (`rule:security/response-body-is-one-typed-member`). Member at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:1826`, card at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:566`. The tests after `framing` already drive it and need only the `covers:` line if they pin the member.

**`Core\Response\Stream::write`** — owes the class card, examples, hostile, perf and 2 tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). Member at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:1898`; the class card goes above the class's `CLASS` row, and the name comes out of `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD` at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs:5279`. As an instance member it needs a `covers:` marker even on a `.nvst` case that calls it.

backlog: A body member called after `sendFile` in one request: the server sends the file and drops the other body (`crates/nvs-server/src/serve.rs`'s `finished`), and `nvs run --request` prints both. Whether a later body member should clear the file name is a question for `nvs_stdlib::response`'s module doc.
`Core\Test::request` against a handler that calls `sendFile`: `runner.rs`'s `UnderTest` never reads the completion's `file_body`, so the test response's body is probably empty. Not checked.
